speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: It split when it took the kennel stone by the well. The pin holds. The box of the hub is too wide for it now.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Set it on the bench. Let me see the pin.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: If you pare the pin thinner it will wobble worse than it did before dinner.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not paring the pin, Judith. I am looking at the ash.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: You have the paring-knife in your hand. Men with a knife pare things until they are too small, and then they say the wood was bad.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: Hold thy tongue, Judith. He has not cut it yet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: There are two cracks in the nave, half an inch apart. If I drive a second wooden wedge between them, I split the hub clean in two.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: There. I said it would split.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: It has not split. He said if he drove a wedge. What if we bind it round the outside with pack-thread?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Pack-thread will fray on the gravel in three turns of the yard. Wait. Let me think what fills a gap without wedging it open.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: While you think, the afternoon goes. Uncle Richard would have mended it or thrown it on the fire by now.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Uncle Richard has his own bench at the other end of the room. Thou art welcome to carry the wheel to him.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: No. Keep it here. This is the bench that said it would look.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Wrap the pin, not the wood. Three turns and pare the tail flush.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A leather shim. Look you, children, your aunt has more joinery in her little finger than the whole company of players in Shoreditch.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Keep thy speeches for Shoreditch and cut the leather straight. The knife is dull at the point. Use the heel.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The heel it is. Hold the rim steady, Hamnet, both hands, and do not lean thy chin on my wrist.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: You are cutting it thicker on the left side than the right.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leather gives when the pin goes home. Watch.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: It holds. Give it here. Let me try it on the plank.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Look at it dip. Left, right, left. It goes like a duck with a sore foot.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: It goes every time. Watch it down the yard to the pear tree.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Unevenly. I told you from the start it would turn unevenly, and so it does.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: It turns till supper, and that is all a boy's wheel owes anybody.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Aye. Leave the scrap on the bench, Joan. The kennel stone may want a second bout.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: It did turn. It turned too far, and it came back. I am taking it to the pear tree and back.
